title: need advice, should I keep working on the presentation?
author: dantemp

comments.author: dantemp
comments.body: Working on a world-sim game, generally a genre where AAA presentation is non-existent so I'm hoping that even sub-par presentation isn't going to feel super bad. Do you guys think this level is acceptable?

replies.author: Aeweisafemalesheep
replies.body: I don't really think this has great style nor art direction dude. Sorry. Without reading your comment I had no idea what was going on either.

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: I lack any confidence in my ability to direct art, that's why I'm asking for people to help me judge, thanks for sharing your opinion.

replies.author: Aeweisafemalesheep
replies.body: This may be something where you hire an artist, like a concept artist and contract them to give you work in a specific tone or style to train something on in return for some fair contract down the line and also an upfront so you can get some aspect of style or visual tone set.

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: i'd love to be able to spend money on that, I hope I get the game to a decent level, manage to get any sales and any money I make go right back into investing in the quality of the game.

replies.author: Aeweisafemalesheep
replies.body:
You're looking at a tough market if you're going to sloperate there. If say 3 of a similar game come out on steam and one just has the brand or marketing we can say common sense stuff. Now what about when 10, 50, 100, 1k? Of a game or similar genre/family happen and some have an IP or a brand.

you're esentially making a prototype.

and youre entering whatever into a possibly saturated market.

whatever youre spending on tokenization. i dunno if prototypes can even make that back before the slopwave. Now. If i make a generic RTS and it's like a 7. Where Tempest Rising could sell their good game for 30 or 40. Maybe i can sell a near clone or a variant for 13? 12? And steam sale into 7.99? If i am lucky. And who says i'll make anything if i tag it ai and don't do good mechanics and it also looks meh.

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body:
well yeah, that's why I want to get the presentation to the best possible state with my current abilities and tools, this thread is already giving me interesting ideas to try, can't wait for my usage to reset and test if they'll work. 

also I'm not confident about my art direction skills but I'm super confident about my gameplay direction skills, which is why I'm working on this in the first place. If I'm not delusional about it hopefully fun gameplay for an underserved niche will give me some success. I don't need to be the next 10m copies game to be happy about it.

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: I had claude fable steer my local models (can't even tell you which one it used, probably flux) to create a reference image for feasible game art  for my game (it's a world sim so zoomed overhead view is acceptable so I can get away with tiny imperfections that are not visible at the distance). Then it created it on its own trying to match the image. I think it used all sorts of stuff, different elements were made different ways. Basically find a look you'll be aiming for and then ask the AI what it needs to achieve it. If you don't have a pc that can run local models (I'm running a 4090) there are cheap services that give you access to all sorts of image generators 3d model generators that you can connect claude to. The most expensive part is running this on fable, I'm on the ultra plan (200 bucks a month) and I burned through a week's worth of usage for Fable in a day, and it still has a lot of work. What you are seeing is like the 6th pass.

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: Another thing I forgot to mention that is very important. Set it up so one agent builds and another agent reviews and directs fixes. Otherwise after each round you have to find faults on your own and point them out, which gets exhausting. That makes it more expensive usage wise tho

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body:
thanks, glad you think that it looks good

my process was pretty standard I think. I picked a reference generated by an image model:

https://i.redd.it/mnfpdfekum2i1.png

Then told fable to try to match it. It used different techniques, including generating textures using my local image generators, I think it used flux. Then it kept giving me results I wasn't really happy with and I asked it to keep improving by pointing what I don't like. That's how I arrived at the left image. Then I decided to try astra because I heard that it's good at 3d modelling. I told it to just get closer to the reference image and it got me this. TBH it isn't perfect, in the reference there's a wave spread as if a stone is thrown there and it made it add a stationary wave for no reason. But it made the grass so much closer to the reference it's unreal, not sure what fable was doing there. Also it added clouds which I don't know if I like because it does make it look better but if I'm going to have it in the game I'll have to design a weather system lmao

P.S. The scene is built in godot.

Edit: actually the grass was one point where I had to go "the grass in the reference is much denser and brighter than what you are doing, try to match it" and that gave me the biggest jump. As for the lighting I think the cloud effect is what actually did the trick.
